title: Bhabha, Achebe and Hybridity
welcome_lead: From Bhabha's third space to Achebe's polemic — survey post-colonial concepts of mixture, mimicry and writing back.
meta_desc: Bhabha's hybridity, mimicry and Achebe on Conrad at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You have toured post-colonial concepts of hybridity, mimicry and the counter-discursive — empire answered back.

walkthroughs.h2: Almost the Same but Not Quite
walkthroughs.body_html: Bhabha argues colonial authority demands the colonised resemble the coloniser but not exactly. Mimicry preserves and destabilises that authority at once.

Achebe's 1975 lecture 'An Image of Africa' argued Heart of Darkness depended on dehumanising African presence.

The lecture reframed Conrad's reception and helped institutionalise post-colonial criticism.
Jean Rhys's Wide Sargasso Sea (1966) gives Bertha Mason from Jane Eyre a Caribbean voice and prehistory — writing back at its most architectural.

Why does historical context matter when reading literature?
options: Context just means writing about what the author had for breakfast.
Texts emerge from and respond to specific historical conditions — context illuminates references, assumptions and arguments that might otherwise be invisible.
Context is required because all texts are about history.
Genre means whether a book is fiction or non-fiction.

mcqs.q: Why are genre conventions important when interpreting a text?
options: Context is required because all texts are about history.
Genre is just a label to help bookshops categorise novels.
Genre means whether a book is fiction or non-fiction.
They set reader expectations the text can fulfil or subvert; analysing how a text uses or breaks conventions reveals its meaning and significance.

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.
It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
